column3: Near-exact maghfirah and ajr outcome parallel, joined to inward khashyah.
No distinct addition to 49:3 beyond a remote seed-cover channel resonance.
Adds a heart-directed response under trial, without the voice or messenger setting.
Near-exact maghfirah and great-ajr formula for faithful, righteous conduct.
Immediate boundary for voice and speech in the Prophet's presence.
Adds an enduring ajr frame, but lacks the tested-heart and restraint setting.
Directly parallels ghadd as disciplined access-control linked with inner purification.
Extends the Messenger-among-you setting with inwardly formed faith and aversion to deviation.
Only repeats an unending ajr outcome already supplied more specifically above.
Adds patience and righteous action to the repeated maghfirah-and-ajr outcome pattern.
No clear contribution to the focus's restraint, heart-testing, or outcome frame.
At most supplies a divine-oversight setting for plans, not the focus's ethical relation.
Contrasts rejection with the familiar faithful-conduct, maghfirah, and ajr outcome.
Completes the adjacent account by locating the preceding formation in divine fadl and ni'mah.
Frames maghfirah within divine ownership and judgment, without the focus's interpersonal setting.
A contrary heart condition sharpens the significance of a heart prepared for taqwa.
Carries restraint into just repair when communal conflict breaks out.
Tests the credibility of speech by conduct under the divine evaluative standpoint.
Connects companionship with the Messenger, communal devotion, and the same final formula.
No distinct contribution to the focus's ethical or heart-testing frame.
Only a remote proximity-to-source resonance; it does not develop the focus.
Links divine knowledge of hearts with a targeted, weighty mode of address.
Broadens disciplined social speech into suspicion, intrusion, and harmful talk, with taqwa.
Distinguishes verbal claim from faith entering hearts and retains forgiveness as open development.
Directly separates mouth-level claim from inward faith, clarifying the focus on hearts.
Offers received honor as a counterweight to self-elevation, indirectly supporting humble carriage.
Explicitly pairs taqwa and maghfirah as complementary divine protection.
Reinforces warning, unseen khashyah, maghfirah, and noble ajr, though it is redundant.
Immediate companion card: patient waiting at the Prophet's threshold and maghfirah.
Joins taqwa, faith in the Messenger, mercy, guidance, and maghfirah in one progression.
Adds a hostile use of proximity to the Messenger, but not the focus's self-restraint.
Supplies taqwa under impending upheaval, without a specific route to the focus.
Clarifies testing as limited human evidence while Allah alone knows inward faith.
Shows outward deviation feeding an inward turn away in a Messenger-facing setting.
Extends surah social discipline to ridicule and naming, yet is less direct than the voice cards.
Near-direct parallel: measured bearing and lowered voice as one disciplined calibration.
Only a broad fear-and-greatness contrast; no distinct focus route appears.
No distinct addition beyond a remote channel association.
Pairs ajr with taqwa after pressure and changed status, adding durability of restraint.
Places outward reverence in taqwa of hearts, strongly parallel to the focus's inward basis.
Adds careful verification before speech-driven harm within the same surah's discipline.
No distinct addition to the focus beyond a general divine-accounting setting.
Shows justice under antipathy as conduct brought near to taqwa.
Pairs avoidance of grave wrongs with forgiveness amid anger, an adjacent restraint pattern.
Marks a limit on human knowledge before Allah, only indirectly related to the focus.
Adds patient devotion and taqwa as an end-state, but no close focus relation.
Immediate contrary example of calling from behind the chambers without due understanding.
No distinct addition to the focus's voice, heart, taqwa, or outcome frame.
A Messenger-facing rejection scene, but it does not illuminate the focus's restraint.
Reiterates faithful action with maghfirah and honorable provision; its repair channel is secondary.
A bare taqwa summons adds little after the stronger taqwa cards.
Uses relinquishment and remembered favor to illustrate a practical path nearer taqwa.
Locates true honor in taqwa under Allah's knowing evaluation, countering status display.
Only supplies the eventual setting of the muttaqun, already well covered.
A heart-deviation boundary adds caution about claiming inward certainty or interpretive control.
No distinct addition beyond a remote seed-measure channel association.
Adds giving as conduct joined to taqwa, though the route is general and indirect.
Connects truthfulness and taqwa, but adds little to the focus after earlier cards.
Immediate opening boundary: do not advance before Allah and His Messenger; retain taqwa.
A return-without-harm reading is only a remote parallel to inward formation.
A contrary use of voice as incitement sharpens the boundary around disciplined voice.
Affirms the noble standing of the Messenger; the honor-channel parallel remains indirect.
Shows that mere proximity to a sacred setting does not establish proper conduct.
Closely parallels regulated access, avoidance of harm to the Prophet, and heart purification.
A broad account of self-loss through forgetting adds only a distant deviation boundary.
Presents maghfirah after acknowledged wrong as protection without erasing moral consequence.
Directly concerns ungrounded speech, its gravity before Allah, and communal verbal restraint.
No distinct addition beyond the remote seed-retrieval channel.
The sole route is a contrast reading, so it is not positive support for the focus.
A direct voice parallel: voices are humbled, leaving only the slightest sound.
Supports reverent magnification over self-magnification, but remains abstract.
Tests whether communal direction remains rightly ordered when the Messenger is absent.
A second ghadd-and-guarding parallel, useful but redundant after 24:30.
No distinct addition to the focus's ethical or heart-testing frame.
A warning against being deceived by outward movement offers only a distant corrective.
Joins response to Allah and the Messenger, taqwa, and great ajr after hardship.
A remote contrast with jocular self-regard; no clear focus route is supplied.
The available covering link is explicitly contrast-only, not positive support.
Adds hearts stirred by Allah alongside patience and spending, but not the voice relation.
No distinct addition beyond a weak spatial-proximity resonance.
Contrasts seeking Messenger-linked maghfirah with arrogant turning away.
Reinforces the protective dimension of maghfirah, though it is formulaically sparse.
Links commitment in the Messenger-facing relation to faithful fulfillment and great ajr.
A reversal into humiliation is only a distant contrary parallel.
Reiterates inwardly grounded believer status with stations, maghfirah, and honorable provision.
Connects warning with taqwa through revealed spirit, but lacks the focus's relational setting.
Adds communal sacrifice and support to the recurring maghfirah-and-provision outcome.
No distinct addition to the focus beyond a general divine-time contrast.
A direct contrary response of mockery toward the Messenger clarifies the respect boundary.
Places the Messenger amid those in prostration, a secondary communal-nearness parallel.
Only repeats great ajr in a distinct service comparison, without the focus's central themes.
A contrary trajectory of worsening heart disease sharpens the value of inward testing.
Directly treats covert harmful speech, disobedience to the Messenger, and its grave outcome.
Shows pride blocking a taqwa-directed correction, a useful contrary posture to humility.
A general inward-versus-display warning, too sparse to add much here.
Offers taqwa through cosmic signs, but no close focus relation.
No distinct addition to the focus's voice, heart, or Messenger-facing discipline.
Links visible repair after wrongdoing with renewed maghfirah, extending the restoration side.
No distinct addition beyond a broad taqwa reference in a separate legal setting.
Adds khashyah, divine-nearness, and enduring reward, though it is less specific than earlier parallels.
Direct Messenger-facing speech discipline; its address boundary belongs beside 49:2-5.
Pairs a measured word with maghfirah, extending the verbal-restraint side.
Makes anger-restraint and pardon defining conduct of the muttaqun.
Links gentleness, consultation, and a non-hardened heart in the Prophet-facing community.
Makes Messenger-directed judgment require inward submission, not outward compliance alone.
Sets a boundary on public harmful speech, with a limited exception.
Directly joins inward humility, khashyah, and speech kept below jah r.
Supplies the heart-response and inward awe of those marked as believers.
Joins taqwa with discernment, expiation, and maghfirah.
A contrary case of hurting the Messenger clarifies the protective respect boundary.
A contrary Messenger-facing speech act sharpens the gravity of verbal irreverence.
Commands the best mode of speech and identifies the divisive contrary pressure.
Direct voice-calibration parallel: neither jah r nor concealment, but a measured path.
A quiet address to Allah supplies a secondary low-voice parallel.
Adds turning away from laghw as a neighboring discipline of expression.
Models the believer's response when called by Allah and His Messenger.
Directly distinguishes the Messenger's summons from ordinary interpersonal calling.
Pairs humble carriage with a restrained answer under provocation.
Adds dignified passage through laghw as a complementary social discipline.
Directly regulates qawl in view of a diseased heart and requires recognized speech.
Near-exact convergence of humility, khashyah, maghfirah, and great ajr.
Supplies an explicit communal practice of honoring the Prophet.
A strong contrary boundary: harming Allah and His Messenger has grave consequence.
Uses the harm done to Musa as a warning against harming a Messenger.
Combines taqwa, sound speech, repaired deeds, maghfirah, and obedience to Allah and His Messenger.
Adds a reverent bodily and heart response to divine discourse, then inward softness.
Connects obedience to Allah and the Messenger with preserving rather than voiding deeds.
Explicitly binds belief in the Messenger to support and reverent honoring.
Extends the local passage through fraternal repair and taqwa.
Distinguishes settled belief in Allah and His Messenger from doubt and merely asserted allegiance.
Directly calls believers' hearts toward khushu before Allah's reminder.
Regulates private speech by excluding sin, aggression, and disobedience to the Messenger.
Links taqwa with expiation and magnified ajr.
Supplies the taqwa-fujur polarity at the level of the self, a secondary inward frame.
